content.text:
One correction before the design. Earlier I said the fork added the radius-4 icon button branch to OrcaSlicer's Button.cpp. That was wrong. I had diffed against the merge base with upstream's main branch, which is behind the release branch this fork actually starts from. Against the true base, Button.cpp has no fork changes. That branch is upstream code, so it is not a rule violation and not ours to fix.

## Recommendation: grow the loader that already exists

The simplest design is to make `ShellTheme` the single source for every token group, not only colour. It already parses the JSON, already throws loudly if the file is missing, and is already passed by reference into every shell widget. Nothing new has to be invented, only three things added.

**1. Parse the other three token groups.** Alongside `palette(dark)`, expose two more accessors:

- `metrics()` returns a small struct with the three radii, the spacing steps, and the button recipes, all in DIP. Callers still wrap values in `FromDIP()` because that must be done per window.
- `font(TextRole)` returns a cached wxFont for exactly five roles: page title, section, body, label, metadata, plus one technical role for the teletype face. Fonts are built through OrcaSlicer's public `Label::sysFont(size, bold)`, which already handles the HarmonyOS face, the Korean fallback, and the platform size fudge.

Because the role enum has only those names, a widget cannot ask for "bold 14". The off-scale cases disappear at compile time instead of in review.

**2. Load it once.** Today the file is parsed twice, once as a static in BrandPalette and once as a member of ShellController. Load it in the brand layer and hand ShellController the same instance. Keep passing `const ShellTheme&` into widgets as now. That stays explicit and testable.

**3. Put component recipes in one fork-owned file.** A handful of free functions such as `style_button(Button&, ButtonRole, theme)` set min size, padding, radius, font, and the StateColor tables from the palette and metrics. They use only upstream's public setters, so no OrcaSlicer line changes. The Retry button, the MCP dialog buttons, and the spool fields become one call each. Custom-painted widgets like the header chips read `metrics().radius_standard` directly.

## What to leave alone

- **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces keep radius 4 and their own fonts.** Unlike colour, there is no single funnel for radius in upstream. Each widget calls its own setter, so a hook would not help. Those screens are slated for replacement anyway.
- **Do not generate a C++ header from the JSON at build time.** It adds a build step and a second copy of the truth. The runtime parse already exists.
- **Do not introduce a global theme singleton in widgets.** Reference passing is working and keeps the fake workspace tests simple.
- **Keep the appearance fan-out as is.** `apply_appearance(bool dark)` already reaches every shell widget and the web view.

## Guard it with tests

Extend the existing brand test so it also asserts the dimension and typography tokens are exactly the documented scales. A JSON edit that adds radius 10 then fails the build. Add one small ShellTheme test that the label role resolves to 12 bold and the body role to 14 regular. After that, the only way to get a radius or font in shell code is through the theme, which is the property you asked for.

Rough size: about 60 lines added to ShellTheme, a 40-line recipes file, call-site edits in six shell files, 30 lines of test, and zero upstream lines.
say it again using plain english output style

First, a correction to something I said earlier. I claimed we had added a small "icon button" block with a radius of 4 to one of OrcaSlicer's files. That was wrong. I had compared against the wrong starting point. Against the commit this fork really branches from, that file is untouched. The radius-4 code belongs to OrcaSlicer, so it is not a rule violation and not ours to fix.

## The recommendation

We already have a small C++ class, `ShellTheme`, that reads the design token file at startup and hands out the light and dark colour sets. Every widget we wrote already receives a reference to it. The simplest design is to make that same class the only place any styling value comes from, by teaching it to read the rest of the token file too. Three additions:

- **Read sizes and fonts, not only colours.** Add one accessor that returns the three corner radii and the spacing steps, and another that returns a ready-made font for each of the five text roles the design system allows, plus one for technical text like temperatures. Fonts are built with an OrcaSlicer helper that already knows the product font and its fallbacks. Because the font accessor takes a role name and nothing else, a widget cannot ask for a size and weight the design system does not list. Bad combinations stop compiling.
- **Load the file once.** Right now it is parsed twice, once by the brand code and once by the shell controller. Load it in one place and pass that instance along. Keep passing it into widgets by reference as we do now.
- **Write the button recipes once.** The token file describes each button type, for example "icon button: 26 by 26, radius 6". Put those into a few short helper functions in our own code that set the size, padding, radius, font, and colours on a button in one call. They use only OrcaSlicer's public setters, so no OrcaSlicer file changes. Widgets that draw themselves, like the header chips, read the radius value directly from the theme.

## What not to do

- **Do not try to restyle OrcaSlicer's own screens for radius or font.** Colour worked because OrcaSlicer routes almost every colour through one class we could hook. There is no such choke point for radius or font. Each widget sets its own. Those screens are going to be replaced anyway.
- **Do not generate a C++ header from the JSON during the build.** That adds a build step and a second copy of the truth. Reading the file at startup already works and fails loudly if the file is missing.
- **Do not make the theme a global.** Passing it by reference is working and keeps the test doubles simple.
- **Do not change how dark mode is propagated.** The existing "apply appearance" call already reaches every shell widget and the chat panel.

## How to keep it honest

Extend the existing brand test, which today only checks colour contrast, so it also checks that the radius and text values in the token file are exactly the documented scales. Then a stray radius of 10 fails the build. Add one small test that the theme resolves the "label" role to 12 bold and the "body" role to 14 regular. Once that is in place, the only way for shell code to get a radius or font is through the theme, which is the property you asked for.

Size of the change: roughly 60 lines added to the theme class, a 40-line helper file, small edits in about six shell files, 30 lines of tests, and no OrcaSlicer lines at all.

you said:

3. Put component recipes in one fork-owned file. A handful of free functions such as style_button(Button&, ButtonRole, theme) set min size, padding, radius, font, and the StateColor tables from the palette and metrics.

but you also said: no OrcaSlicer lines at all 

Am I missing anything?

No, both statements hold, but I should have been clearer about what `Button` and `StateColor` are.

`Button` is OrcaSlicer's own button widget class. `StateColor` is OrcaSlicer's small helper type for "one colour per state" (normal, hover, pressed, disabled). Both live in OrcaSlicer files. Our helper functions would *call* them, not *edit* them.

The distinction is between using an upstream class and changing its source:

- **Using it** means our fork-owned file includes OrcaSlicer's header and calls public methods that already exist, such as `SetMinSize`, `SetPaddingSize`, `SetCornerRadius`, `SetFont`, `SetBackgroundColor`, and `SetTextColor`. I checked these are public on `Button` and its base class. Our code is a new file with zero merge cost.
- **Editing it** would mean adding a new method or a new `ButtonType` branch inside Button.cpp itself. That is what the stewardship rules discourage, and it is what the design avoids.

So `style_button` is ordinary caller code. It builds a `StateColor` from our palette values and passes it to the button's existing setter, the same way `AgentWebView.cpp` already calls `SetCornerRadius` on its Retry button today.

The one exposure I mentioned earlier still applies. If OrcaSlicer renames one of those setters, our helper file stops compiling after a rebase. That is a loud, cheap failure rather than a merge conflict, but it is not zero dependency on upstream.
ok. now what's your design for the fork-owned html styles?

The chat panel already does colour the right way. At build time it imports the token JSON, and a small script writes each colour as a CSS variable such as `--action-primary` whenever the host reports light or dark mode. The stylesheet then only ever says `var(--…)` for colour. The gap is that radius and text sizes are typed by hand as `6px` or `14px` across the stylesheet, and nothing stops a `13px` from creeping back in. The design is to give radius and type the same treatment colour already has.

## The recommendation

**1. Emit the dimension and typography tokens as CSS variables too.** Extend [tokens.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/tokens.ts) with a second function that runs once at page start and writes the values that do not change with appearance:

- Three radius variables, `--radius-standard`, `--radius-compact`, `--radius-window`, next to the pill one that already exists.
- One font variable per text role, holding the complete shorthand. For example the body role becomes `--font-body: 400 14px/20px 'HarmonyOS Sans SC', system-ui, sans-serif`. Size, line height, weight, and family travel together, so a rule can no longer change one without the other.

No build step is added. It is the same JSON import the colour code already uses, applied at the same moment, before the first render.

**2. Rewrite the stylesheet to consume them.** Every `border-radius: 6px` becomes `border-radius: var(--radius-standard)`. Every `font-size` and `line-height` pair collapses to one line, `font: var(--font-label)`. The two remaining off-scale values are icon glyphs drawn as text, the paperclip and the remove cross. Replace them with small SVG icons the way the back chevron already works, so they need no font size at all. Colour rules are untouched.

**3. Leave spacing as literal numbers.** Padding and gaps appear in hundreds of places and are all on the 4-to-48 scale already. Wrapping every one in a variable would make the stylesheet harder to read for no gain. A test guards the scale instead.

## Guard it with a test

Add one Vitest case that reads the stylesheet as plain text and fails if it finds a hex or rgb colour, a `border-radius` with a pixel number, a `font-size` or `line-height` declaration outside the font-face block, or a padding, margin, or gap value off the spacing scale. Two cautions from earlier work on this repo: Vitest returns an empty string if you import a CSS file, so read it from disk instead, and inject a violation once to watch the test fail before trusting it.

## What not to do

- **No CSS-in-JS, Tailwind, or CSS modules.** One stylesheet plus variables is the smallest thing that works, and it keeps the bundle a single file, which the web view requires.
- **No generated CSS file checked into the repo.** The runtime variables already exist for colour. Adding a second mechanism for sizes would mean two ways to do the same thing.
- **Do not touch colour.** Every colour reference is already correct.

## Cleanup that goes with it

- Delete `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.css` and `resources/jusprin/branding/brand-tokens.css`. Nothing reads them, and the second one names fonts and radii the design system rejects.
- Mark the [token-sweep handoff](agent-docs/jusprin/agent-panel-token-sweep.md) done, or delete it, and note the new variables in the design-system doc.

Size: about 30 lines in the token script, mechanical edits to roughly 80 lines of the stylesheet, two small SVG icons, and a 40-line test. Rebuild and commit the bundle, since the app loads the committed file.

content.text:
Mostly yes. The file is a plain nested map of names to values, which is the easiest possible shape for both readers. The C++ side walks it with a JSON library and the web side imports it directly, and neither needs a schema library or a code generator. Values are unitless device-independent pixels, so C++ scales them per window and the web side appends `px`. I would keep the overall shape. Five things in it are worth fixing, and none of them requires changing the shape.

- **Light and dark are two separate trees**, so a token can exist in one mode and not the other. The build test only checks that every light token has a dark twin, not the reverse. Today `text.tertiary` exists in dark mode only and slips through. The cheap fix is to check both directions in the test. The thorough fix is to put both modes on each token, for example `"canvas": {"light": "#FFFFFF", "dark": "#17131F"}`, so a missing mode is visible in the file itself. That changes about ten lines on each reader. I would take the cheap fix now and the thorough one only if the palette starts growing.
- **The header claims a standard it does not follow.** The `$schema` line points at the W3C design-tokens format, but that format wraps every value in `$value` and `$type` and this file does not. Either drop the line or adopt the format. Adopting it makes both readers more verbose and only pays off if the tokens are going to round-trip through Figma variables or a tool like Style Dictionary. Unless that is planned, drop the line.
- **The button recipes name their text inconsistently.** Some say `textRole: "metadata"` and others say `textSize: 12`. Every recipe should reference a role, so the C++ font accessor and the web font variables can resolve it the same way. Raw sizes in recipes are how off-scale values sneak in.
- **The font fallback is prose.** "system GUI font" is not something the web side can put in a CSS stack. Add a machine-usable `cssFallback` such as `system-ui, sans-serif`. The C++ side ignores it.
- **There is a second token file that contradicts this one.** `branding/brand-tokens.json` repeats the primitive palette and then specifies Avenir Next, Menlo, and radii of 12, 20, and 24, all of which the design system rejects. Nothing reads it. Delete it along with the two dead CSS exports. The `primitive` block inside the main file is fine to keep, since the rule against using it directly is enforced by review and the fact that neither reader exposes it.

Two things I would not change. The unitless numbers are right for a native app that must handle display scaling. And the small `rules` block of prose at the bottom is harmless documentation that travels with the values.
Write the button recipes once - Doesn't mean that we for change all fork-owned c++ files to use those recipes? but we leave upstream-owned files along?

Yes, exactly that.

The recipes are for the places where our own code creates one of OrcaSlicer's widget classes. Today that is a handful of sites: the Retry button in the Agent web view, the buttons in the MCP connection dialog, and the fields in the spool menu. Each of those currently sets its own font, radius, and colours by hand. They would call one recipe function instead. Widgets we paint ourselves, like the header chips, do not need a recipe. They read the radius and font straight from the theme.

OrcaSlicer's own files stay as they are. Preferences, the settings tabs, and the stock dialogs keep calling OrcaSlicer's `SetStyle` with OrcaSlicer's defaults, which means radius 4 and its own font presets. We do not touch them.

The visible consequence is that an OrcaSlicer dialog next to one of ours will have slightly different corners and type. That matches the position the docs already take for the surfaces that were left teal: they are slated to be hidden or replaced, so editing them now would be permanent merge cost with no lasting value. If that mismatch ever becomes unacceptable before those surfaces are replaced, the only acceptable route would be one small neutral hook in OrcaSlicer's button class, something like a settable default corner radius, in the same spirit as the colour override hook. I would not add it now.

Only where there is real repetition, and I counted rather than guessed. Across our shell and Agent code, the widgets we create from OrcaSlicer or wxWidgets classes are:

| Widget | Sites |
|---|---|
| Static text label | 10 |
| Text input field | 5 |
| Button | 1 |
| Separator line | 1 |

So the honest answer is that a button recipe is the least useful one today. It covers a single site, the Retry button. The two recipes that would actually remove repeated hand-styling are:

- **A label recipe** that takes a text role and a palette colour and applies font and foreground colour. Ten sites, spread over five files, each currently picking a font preset and a colour by hand.
- **A text-field recipe** that applies the body font, the standard radius where the control supports it, and the input colours. Five sites, most of them in the MCP connection dialog, which is the one shell surface that barely touches the palette at all.

Keep all of them in the same small file, and add a button recipe alongside them only because it costs a few lines and the next button will otherwise be styled by hand again.

The rule of thumb going forward: write a recipe when the same upstream widget appears in three or more places in our code with the same intended look. Below that, calling the theme's font and radius accessors at the site is simpler than a function nobody else uses. Our own custom-painted classes, the header buttons and menus, already take the theme in their constructor and do not need recipes at all.

Below is every place the JusPrin design system differs from what OrcaSlicer's own widget code does, measured from the upstream source rather than from the docs. Colour is included briefly for completeness. Everything else is a dimension or behaviour difference.

**Colour**

- OrcaSlicer's brand accent is teal; JusPrin's is purple, swapping to pink in dark mode.
- OrcaSlicer's neutrals are plain greys. JusPrin's are purple-tinted, both light and dark.
- OrcaSlicer derives most dark-mode colours by an automatic lightness inversion in LAB colour space, with a small exception map. JusPrin hand-picks every dark value. Our override table runs before OrcaSlicer's inversion, so it wins wherever a literal is listed.

**Corner radius**

| Widget | OrcaSlicer | JusPrin |
|---|---|---|
| Choice, parameter, icon, expanded buttons | 4 | 6 |
| Compact button | 8 | 8 |
| Window button | 12 | 12 |
| Generic box default | 8 | 6 or 12 by role |
| Text and spin inputs | 0 | 6 |
| Tab control | 5 | not defined |
| Switch | pill | pill |

The button recipes in our token file are OrcaSlicer's own six button types copied with only the radius changed from 4 to 6. Sizes, padding, and text sizes are identical.

**Type**

- OrcaSlicer's most-used size is 13, with over 200 regular and about 40 bold uses. JusPrin has no 13 at all.
- OrcaSlicer uses bold 14 about 120 times. JusPrin's roles have 14 regular only. Our own shell code still uses bold 14 in four places.
- OrcaSlicer uses regular 12 about 130 times. JusPrin's 12 is bold only. Our shell code uses regular 12 ten times.
- OrcaSlicer also uses 9, 11, 15, 16, and 20. None are JusPrin roles.
- JusPrin specifies a line height per role. OrcaSlicer has no line-height concept, and neither does wxWidgets for labels, so this only takes effect on the web panel.
- The font face is the same, HarmonyOS Sans SC. OrcaSlicer shrinks every point size by a fifth on Windows and Linux, and since we build fonts through the same helper, that applies to us too.

**Spacing**

- OrcaSlicer spaces on a 5-step grid: its most common values are 5, 10, 20, 15, 25, and 30. JusPrin uses a 4-step grid: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. Only 20 and 40 appear on both. Our shell code already follows the 4-step grid.

**Icon sizes**

- OrcaSlicer draws functional icons most often at 20, 18, 16, 14, and 12. JusPrin allows 16, 20, and 24 only. 18, 14, and 12 have no JusPrin equivalent.

**Focus**

- OrcaSlicer shows keyboard focus on a button by recolouring its 1-pixel border to teal. JusPrin requires a separate visible 2-pixel ring offset from the control, and says a colour change alone is not enough. Our shell widgets and the web panel implement the ring. Retained OrcaSlicer controls do not.

**Border**

- OrcaSlicer buttons carry a 1-pixel border in every state. JusPrin's token file does not state a border width, so our recipes inherit 1 by default.

**Menus**

- JusPrin gives menu rows no radius inside an 8-radius popover. OrcaSlicer's popups vary by dialog.

**What is not different**

- The font face, the compact and window button recipes, the pill shape for switches and chips, and the use of device-independent pixels are all the same on both sides.

`StaticBox` is OrcaSlicer's base class for its custom-drawn widgets. It is a plain panel that paints its own rounded background and border, and its constructor sets the corner radius to 8 unless the caller overrides it.

It shows up in two ways:

- **As a base class.** Buttons, tab controls, step controls, switch buttons, and the printer info box all inherit from it. Most of those set their own radius, which is why buttons end up at 4 or 12 rather than 8.
- **Used directly** as a rounded container. There are 33 such sites in upstream code, in places like the sidebar parameter panels, the printer status panel, calibration pages, and the machine-selection dialog. Those mostly keep the default 8 or call the setter with 0, 5, 10, or 12.

One correction to my table. I wrote "6 or 12 by role" for JusPrin, but the token file has no entry for a container box. The design system says 6 is the standard control radius and 12 is for large surfaces, so a box would be one of those depending on what it holds, but that is my reading of the rules rather than a value written in the file. If we want a fixed answer, the token file needs a container entry.
Generic box default = StaticBox ? If so, why did you call it Generic box default ?

Yes, the same thing. I renamed it in the table because the plain-English output style asks me to avoid code names in prose, and I judged "generic box" a friendlier label than `StaticBox`. That was the wrong call. The name is the only way to find the class, and inventing a label for it made the table harder to verify, not easier. I should have written `StaticBox` and explained in one clause what it is.

Same applies to the JusPrin column for that row. I filled in "6 or 12" from the design rules, not from a token that exists. The accurate row is:

| Widget | OrcaSlicer | JusPrin |
|---|---|---|
| `StaticBox` default, the rounded container OrcaSlicer's custom widgets inherit from | 8 | no token defined |
but previously you said Jusprin is 6 or 12 by role

Yes, and that earlier value was an inference presented as a fact. I should have labelled it.

What is actually in the token file: three named radii, standard 6, compact 8, window 12, and six button recipes. There is no entry for a container or box.

What I did: I read the design-system doc's descriptions, "6 for standard controls, 12 for window actions and large dialogs", and concluded a box would take one of those depending on what it holds. That is a reasonable reading of the rules, but no token says it, and nothing in our code implements it. So "6 or 12 by role" was my hypothesis, and the table should have said so.

The corrected answer stands: OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` defaults to 8, and JusPrin has no defined value for the equivalent. If we want one, it has to be added to the token file as a decision, and that is a design call rather than something I can derive.

content.text:
The design system now uses a 4-pixel radius for standard controls and an 8-pixel radius for containers, matching OrcaSlicer's own widgets. Seven files changed, nothing is committed, and the native C++ side was not compiled.

**Files changed**

- [design-tokens.json](resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json). Standard radius 6 to 4. New `container` radius of 8. The choice, parameter, icon, and expanded button recipes 6 to 4. Compact stays 8 and window stays 12, which already matched OrcaSlicer.
- [design-system.md](agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md). The radius scale and the four button entries updated, plus a new container line that names OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` default as the reference.
- [agent-panel-token-sweep.md](agent-docs/jusprin/agent-panel-token-sweep.md). The old handoff note said standard had just moved to 6. Two sentences corrected so the doc no longer contradicts the token file.
- [HeaderControls.cpp:323](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:323). The header chips and buttons drew their standard corners at 6. Now 4. The compact print action stays 8 and menu rows stay square.
- [SpoolMenu.cpp:374](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SpoolMenu.cpp:374). The colour swatch corners in the new-spool panel, 6 to 4.
- [styles.css](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css). All 16 standard-control radii in the chat panel, 6px to 4px, and the comment listing the scale. The cards already used 8, which is now the container value, so they did not change.
- [index.html](resources/jusprin/agent/index.html). The committed web bundle, rebuilt from the stylesheet above. The app loads this file, so it has to travel with the source change.

**What was verified**

- The Agent UI build succeeded and all 65 Vitest cases pass. The rebuilt bundle contains 16 four-pixel radii and no six-pixel ones.
- The two C++ edits are integer literals inside existing calls and were not compiled. The only native build on this machine belongs to the main checkout, not this worktree, so it would have compiled the wrong sources. The brand token test checks colour contrast only and is unaffected.

**Left alone on purpose**

- The header chip was drawn at 6 to match the Figma chip component. It now follows the standard radius at 4, since keeping it at 6 would have left the system with a standard value nothing used. If the chip should stay at 6 to match Figma, that is a one-line revert in HeaderControls.
- Retained OrcaSlicer screens were already at 4 and 8, which is the point of the change.

=== commit that settled radius at 6 ===
Follow the design-system components, and settle the standard radius at 6

Measuring the Figma components rather than the screens that use them turned up
values the code had wrong, and one the design system had two answers for.

The chip is 28 tall, not 26. The component is 28 and so was the Toolbar Chip it
replaces; only the screen instances say 26. Menu rows are 36, not 32 -- the
component is 36, and the 26 quoted in the brief exists nowhere. Rows carry no
corner radius and run the full width of the popover, whose 8 is the only
rounding; they were inset by 4 and rounded again. Popover padding is 8 top and
bottom with 2 between rows, none at the sides.

The radius disagreement was real: the old chip said 4, the new one 6, and the
token file said 4 was standard. Rather than force the new chip down to 4, 6
becomes the standard -- it is what the current design draws, and it is already
what five places in the Agent panel use. Changed in the token file, in the
design-system document, and in the header and swatch painting. Compact stays 8
and window stays 12.

The Machine and Spool icons are gone. Machine was the old chip's glyph and
nothing draws it now; Spool was added for a chip half that ended up using a
colour dot instead.

The appearance capture now also requires the chip to be unfocused. It only
checked for an open menu, so the keyboard test running before it left a focus
ring in the saved image -- the third time an appearance check has been narrower
than what it claimed to show. A focused capture now fails the build.

Adds agent-docs/jusprin/agent-panel-token-sweep.md: the Agent panel still uses
type sizes and radii that are not in the system, measured and scoped for a
=== chip commit ===
Fix the chip menus crashing, and match the design's chip

Picking anything that closed a chip menu killed the application. HeaderMenu
destroys the popup before it invokes a row's callback, so the menu controller
was freed while a queued callback still held a pointer to it. Choosing a spool,
a plate, a nozzle, or "Use this spool" was a use-after-free every time.

The controllers are shared now, and every row callback holds a reference, so a
controller outlives its popup by exactly as long as the callbacks need. The
popup handle is weak in return, because a transient popup can be dismissed by
the system at any moment and every step has to tolerate finding it gone.

Two more ways the same lifetime confusion showed up:

Rename and Change colour opened modal dialogs owned by the popup. The system
colour panel has no accept or cancel button of its own on macOS, so its window
frame is the only way out -- and the popup rendered above it, covering exactly
that frame. Anyone who opened it was stuck with no way back. Both rows now
close the menu first and reopen the spool list afterwards.

content.text:
The Figma file "JusPrin v2" defines radius in two places, and only one of them matters. There is a Radius variable collection, but no component is bound to it, so every component carries its own typed number. Updating the variables alone would change nothing on the mockups. The prompt below tells the Figma agent to fix the values and bind them so this does not recur. I left the file open in the Chrome tab.

**Where radius is defined in Figma**

- Variables panel, "Radius" collection: small 6, medium 8, large 12, chip 6, full 10.
- "Design System" page, each component's Appearance block. Measured values:

| Component | Figma today | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| Button/Secondary, Button/Icon | 6 | 4 |
| Segmented Control, Chip/Printer+Spool, Tooltip | 6 | 4 |
| Swatch | 5 | 4 |
| Button/Primary | 8 | 8 |
| Pinned Setup Card, Menu/Popover, Chat Bubble | 8 | 8 |
| Sheet | 12 | 12 |
| Menu/Row, Chat Header | 0 | 0 |
| Field/Search, Composer | 8 | 4, see note |

Containers were already 8 in Figma, so the StaticBox change only needs the variable and the bindings. The Field/Search and Composer rows are inputs. In code they are controls at 4. Figma has them at 8. The prompt treats them as controls to match code, and calls it out so you can veto.

**About the "places left for Figma"**

Nothing in code was left at 6. The header chip was the one site tied to the Figma chip component, and the earlier change already moved it to 4. The prompt below moves the Figma chip variable to 4 to match. If you would rather keep the chip at 6 on both sides, say so and I will revert that one line in HeaderControls.

**Prompt for the Figma agent**

```text
In this file (JusPrin v2), align corner radii with the product code and make
them maintainable. Work on the "Design System" page first, then every other page.

1. Radius variables. In the "Radius" collection set:
   - small: 4 (was 6). This is the standard control radius.
   - chip: 4 (was 6).
   - medium: 8, large: 12, full: 10 — leave unchanged.
   Add a description to "medium": "Containers: cards, popovers, bubbles."

2. Bind every component's corner radius to a variable instead of a typed
   number. Use this mapping:
   - radius/small (4): Button/Secondary, Button/Icon, Segmented Control,
     Tooltip, Swatch, Field/Search, Composer.
   - radius/chip (4): Chip/Printer+Spool and Chip/Printer+Spool · Dark,
     all variants.
   - radius/medium (8): Button/Primary, Pinned Setup Card, Menu/Popover,
     Chat Bubble.
   - radius/large (12): Sheet.
   - Leave Menu/Row, Chat Header, Stepper, and Status Dot at 0.
   Bind on every variant, not only the default one. Do not change any other
   property of these components.

3. Swatch also has a hard-coded fill 33B2A6. Replace it with a Color
   Primitive or Semantic Color variable; do not leave a raw hex.

4. On every page, find frames or rectangles that are not component
   instances and have a corner radius of 5 or 6. For each, bind it to
   radius/small if it draws a control, radius/medium if it draws a
   container, and list anything you were unsure about instead of guessing.

5. Report back: every node you changed, grouped by page, with old and new
   value, and the list from step 4 that you did not touch.
```

**One thing I noticed but did not act on**

Figma's text styles include sizes the code design system does not have. Control Bold, Button Label, Chat Message, and Mono Body are all 13/18, and Mono Label and Link Small are 11/16. That is the same drift the radius had, in the other direction. It is a separate decision.

The cherry-pick is done and the inventory is refreshed. Here is the outcome and the recommendations.

**Landed on jusprin-newui** as `a5e5c2fffa`. Three files conflicted with the 11 newer commits there. The header code dropped out of the commit entirely because `jusprin-newui` had already moved the header to radius 4 in an earlier revert. The stylesheet conflict was one comment line. The bundle was rebuilt from the merged stylesheet, and all 96 Vitest cases pass on that branch. The main checkout's working tree is clean.

## Recommended changes, C++ side

Colour is already clean: outside the brand mapping table and the filament colour-name list, there is no colour literal in fork-owned C++. The remaining hard-coding is fonts, radii, and sizes. Ranked by value:

1. **Add font roles to `ShellTheme`.** Twenty-six call sites pick an OrcaSlicer font preset by hand, sixteen of them in HeaderControls, and four of those pick combinations the design system does not define. Give the theme a `font(TextRole)` accessor with exactly the five roles plus technical, built through OrcaSlicer's existing font helper. Off-scale choices then fail to compile.
2. **Add radius and spacing to `ShellTheme`.** Four sites draw a rounded rectangle from a literal, and about 100 sites call `FromDIP` with a bare number. Parse the token file's dimension block into a small struct and expose `metrics().radius_standard` and friends. Spacing can stay literal where it is on the scale, but radius should never be typed again.
3. **Load the theme once.** BrandPalette and ShellController each parse the JSON. Load it in the brand layer and pass that instance to the shell.
4. **Write three recipes** in one fork-owned file: label (role plus palette colour), text field, and button. They cover ten static-text sites, five input sites, and one button, and use only upstream's public setters. The MCP connection dialog is the main beneficiary, since it barely touches the palette today.
5. **Move component dimensions into the token file.** The chip is 28 tall, menu rows 36, the status row 34, the swatch cell 24. These live as literals in the shell today and nowhere in the tokens, so Figma and code can drift apart silently. Add a `component` entry for each and read it through the theme.

## Recommended changes, HTML and JS side

Colour is clean here too: zero hex or rgb literals, everything through `var(--…)`. The work is sizes.

1. **Emit radius and font tokens as CSS variables** from the existing `tokens.ts`, once at page start. Three radius variables plus one `--font-<role>` shorthand per text role that carries size, line height, weight, and family together.
2. **Replace the literals.** Thirty-one radius declarations become `var(--radius-…)`. Fifty-six `font-size` and fifty `line-height` declarations collapse into one `font: var(--font-…)` line each. Three sizes are off-scale today: a 9px added by the setup card, and the 20px and 16px icon glyphs. Replace the glyphs with SVG masks the way the back chevron already works.
3. **Fold the monospace stack into the tokens.** The stylesheet now declares `--mono` locally with a platform font list. Add a `technical` family entry to the token JSON so the web and native sides name the same thing.
4. **Leave spacing literal.** Padding and gap values appear in over a hundred places and are on the scale. A test guards them instead.

## Guard both sides

- Extend the brand test so the dimension and typography tokens must equal the documented scales. A stray 5 or 13 in the JSON fails the build.
- Add one ShellTheme test that the label role is 12 bold and body is 14 regular.
- Add one Vitest case that reads the stylesheet from disk and fails on any hex colour, any pixel `border-radius`, any `font-size` or `line-height` outside the font-face block, or any spacing value off the 4-step scale. Inject a violation once to prove it fails before trusting it.
- Delete the two dead CSS token exports and the contradictory brand-tokens JSON.

Suggested order: guards and token JSON first, then the web side in two commits (variables, then the sweep), then the C++ theme accessors, then the recipes. No upstream OrcaSlicer line changes in any of it.
can you divide the work to up to 5 subagents? afterward you check their work?

Yes. I'll split it into two rounds so the agents do not fight over the same files: three in parallel first (tokens and guards, the web panel, the native theme), then two more once the theme API has landed (call-site migration, full build and visual check). Before spawning, I'll fix the shared token-file contract myself so all three read the same thing, and pull in the build recipes from memory for the prompts.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac; the App Store copy and other worktree builds share the bundle id, so run a re-signed copy under its own bundle id for screenshots."
metadata:

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

The doc update is committed on the native branch as `8afe684780`, on top of the combined tip. Everything for the sweep is now on one line of seven commits above the guard commit that already landed:

1. Expose the token metrics and text roles through ShellTheme, and load it once

3. Dress every shell widget from the theme, through three recipes
